$comment: The single place the documentation set is described.
The prose itself is never copied here. Every entry points at a file under
docs/ at the workspace root, which stays the one editable copy — the site
reads those files at build time and renders them. Adding a document means
adding it to docs/ and naming it here (or in `internal`), and nothing else.
JSON rather than TypeScript so that `scripts/site-docs.mjs` and the Next
app read the same bytes. A registry the checker cannot parse is a registry
that drifts from what is published.
Checked by `pnpm site:docs:check`, which fails when a file under docs/ is
in neither list, when an entry points at a file that does not exist, or
when README.md's generated table no longer matches this file.

sections.title: Setting up
sections.blurb: What Meith is, a board running on your machine in a minute, and the routes onto a server of your own.

sections.title: Getting started
sections.blurb: The first hour with a running board: the first steps in the admin panel, what the board repository holds, installing plugins and themes, and moving an existing community across.

sections.title: Operating
sections.blurb: For the person minding the server: routine checks, backups, upgrades, monitoring, recovery, sign-in, languages and scaling.

sections.title: Using
sections.blurb: For organisers, moderators and members, from the browser: forums and permissions, groups, moderation, memberships, spam controls and writing posts.

sections.title: Developing
sections.blurb: Extending a board with themes and plugins, the generated references, the architecture, and contributing to Meith itself.

documents.title: Introduction
documents.blurb: The philosophy: server-first pages that work with JavaScript off, a board pinned in a small repository, and a server of your own. Start here to see whether Meith thinks like you do.

documents.title: Quickstart
documents.blurb: npx create-meith, and a minute later a board is running on your machine in fixture mode — no database, no Docker, no account with anybody.

documents.title: Deployment
documents.blurb: The four-service production shape every route deploys, and the chooser: Coolify guided, Compose by hand, or Vercel without a server.

documents.title: Deploying with Coolify
documents.blurb: From a rented server to a board on your own domain, with Coolify, in about twenty minutes. Written for whichever volunteer drew the short straw.

documents.title: Docker Compose by hand
documents.blurb: The advanced route: Docker Compose, a `.env` you write, and a reverse proxy you run. Most boards should deploy with Coolify instead.

documents.title: Running on Vercel
documents.blurb: The board on functions: the driver set, the build command that carries the migration, the cron job that replaces the worker, what previews and rollbacks do to your schema — and how to leave again.

documents.title: First steps
documents.blurb: What to do in the first hour after the installer: sign in, name the board, create the forums, set who may register, appoint the staff, and switch the backups on.

documents.title: Configuration in code
documents.blurb: What the board repository pins — the engine version, the themes, the plugins — and the deliberate line between it and everything organisers run from the browser.

documents.title: Installing plugins and themes
documents.blurb: The board admin's guide to adding a plugin or theme: find one, install the package, register it, redeploy, and manage it from the panel.

documents.title: Migrating from MyBB or phpBB
documents.blurb: The full procedure: what to check first, the import command for each source, what does and does not come across, and what to do after it finishes.

documents.title: MyBB parity decisions
documents.blurb: Every place Meith deliberately behaves differently from MyBB, with the reasoning and the cost. Read it before promising anyone a like-for-like move.

documents.title: phpBB parity decisions
documents.blurb: Where a Meith board imported from phpBB behaves differently from the one it came from — the ACL, warnings, bans, announcements and polls, and a couple of places phpBB's own model already matches Meith's.

documents.title: Operations
documents.blurb: Routine checks, configuration, maintenance commands, backups, recovery, web push, the cookies and security headers the board serves, and troubleshooting for a running board.

documents.title: Backups
documents.blurb: Taking a backup from the control panel, on a schedule, off the server and before an upgrade; what a bundle carries; and restoring one from the installer or the command line.

documents.title: Upgrading a board
documents.blurb: Moving a board between versions: the upgrade command, how far you can jump, and the behaviour changes each release brings.

documents.title: Monitoring & alerting
documents.blurb: Liveness versus readiness, the optional Prometheus metrics endpoint and what to alert on, distributed tracing, and shipping logs.

documents.title: Disaster recovery
documents.blurb: The runbook for the day the server is gone: what recovery consumes, the order of operations from provisioning to DNS, and the rehearsal that turns it from a hope into a plan.

documents.title: Signing in
documents.blurb: Two-factor authentication, federated sign-in and passkeys: what each means for your members, how to configure them, and the record of what has opened an account.

documents.title: Languages
documents.blurb: How a page picks its language, how to add one, and how a theme or plugin ships its own words.

documents.title: Webhooks
documents.blurb: Deliver board events to an endpoint you choose: creating a subscription, the topics and payload formats, verifying a delivery's signature, and how retries and dead-lettering work.

documents.title: Scaling out
documents.blurb: Running more than one web container: the Redis cache that keeps them coherent, what already scales, and the step-by-step migration from a single-instance board.

documents.title: Demo mode
documents.blurb: The self-resetting public demo board that runs at demo.meith.dev — what it changes, and how to run one yourself.

documents.title: The organiser's guide
documents.blurb: Running the board from a browser: forums and the organisers' room, the community's name and colours, announcements, members — and handing it all over.

documents.title: The moderator's guide
documents.blurb: For the volunteers who keep it civil: the approval queue, reports, tidying threads, warnings and bans — and where each screen lives.

documents.title: Forums and permissions
documents.blurb: The board's shape and who may do what inside it: the forum tree, a forum's options, how a permission resolves, the matrix, and what a moderator appointment grants.

documents.title: Groups and promotions
documents.blurb: What a group carries: board-wide permissions, the daily allowances, colours and badges, display groups, the groups a plugin may grant, and the rules that promote members automatically.

documents.title: Spam controls and filters
documents.blurb: The registration challenge, the rate limits and login counters, the render-time word filter, and the ban filters that turn somebody away before an account exists — what each is worth and what it costs a real visitor.

documents.title: Reputation
documents.blurb: Members rating each other: what a rating is worth, the four settings, the two that decide between a one-press thanks and a form, and why the totals cannot drift.

documents.title: Search
documents.blurb: The four controls over the most expensive thing a visitor can ask for: switching search off without losing the index, the shortest word a query may rest on, and the two different limits on how often.

documents.title: The memberships guide
documents.blurb: Taking memberships through the board: plans, discount codes, gifting, the memberships desk and the ledger — Dues end to end, without a terminal.

documents.title: Writing a post
documents.blurb: The composer's toolbar and the syntax behind it: highlighted code, spoilers, mention suggestions, link previews, and placing an attachment inline.

documents.title: Write your first plugin
documents.blurb: The walkthrough from an empty directory to a plugin running inside a board and listed on the marketplace: scaffold, change a hook, test it, install it, publish it.

documents.title: Themes
documents.blurb: How to write a theme, what a theme may do, and what the API freeze covers.

documents.title: Plugins
documents.blurb: What a plugin is, what it may and may not do, and how a failure is contained.

documents.title: The marketplace
documents.blurb: The curated, reviewed feed of plugins and themes: the listing schema, the review bar, the trust it does and does not extend, and how to submit or remove one.

documents.title: REST API v1
documents.blurb: Every endpoint, scope and rate limit, generated from the route registry.

documents.title: Theme slots and view models
documents.blurb: Every slot and every view model, generated from the slot registry.

documents.title: Plugin hooks
documents.blurb: Every hook and payload, generated from the hook registry.

documents.title: Architecture
documents.blurb: How Meith fits together: the processes, the layers, the path a request takes, and the extension seams.

documents.title: Performance
documents.blurb: The p95 budgets for the hot pages, and what the last recorded run measured against a full-scale board.

documents.title: Development
documents.blurb: Running the board on your own machine, the workspace layout, the commands, and what to do before opening a pull request.
